ANDROID-01.impact: - `android/mesh/src/main/java/io/godstone/mesh/transport/BleTransport.kt:312` handles the successful central CCCD action by publishing `Found`, then stops. It does not call `beginTrustedHandshake`. - `BleTransport.kt:1739` defines `beginTrustedHandshake`. Searching both `android/mesh/src/main` and `android/app/src/main` finds its definition and no invocation (`production_entrypoints.txt`). Existing tests call it explicitly, e.g. `ReadinessT21Test.kt:321`. - `BleTransport.kt:1353` defines `beginKeyConfirmation`; every invocation found outside its definition is a test invocation (`keyconfirmation_callers.txt`). Completing HS3 at lines 1566/1623 only emits `handshakeReadyFlow`. - `MeshNode.kt:179` subscribes only to `peers()` and `received()`. It subscribes to neither handshake-ready nor application-link-ready events and does not perform D2/key confirmation itself. Failure schedule: two genuine devices finish discovery, LinkInfo exchange, and CCCD setup. The central produces `PublishFound`; no HS1 is sent. The responder cannot initiate Noise XX. Both remain physically bound without a trusted session. If a test or later caller manually starts D2, nothing automatically begins the mandatory encrypted confirmation round afterward.

ANDROID-03.impact: - `PeerEventPublisher.kt:47` and `TrustedPeerChannel.kt` implement new types. Production source search finds no instantiation of `PeerEventPublisher` and no `TrustedPeer.capture` call. - `BleTransport.kt:589` adds a relation to `publishedRelations` and at line 596 performs unchecked `peerEventsFlow.tryEmit(PeerEvent.Found(peerMacBytes,...))`. This is invoked at physical readiness, before authentication. `unpublishRelation` at line 614 similarly ignores Lost emission failure. - `MeshNode.kt:199` keys its peer map from `event.peerId` and line 181 forwards `received()` pairs into `handleInboundFrame`. `Transport.kt` still exposes `Flow<Pair<ByteArray, ByteArray>>`, not an authenticated relation-bearing frame. - `BleTransport.kt:1118` decrypts using the queued byte-array peer handle and line 1127 calls unchecked `trySend(peerId to plaintext)`. It carries no immutable authenticated identity/trust version for delayed delivery. - Even the separate `publishApplicationLinkReadyOnce` at line 1328 uses a replay-zero SharedFlow. A `tryEmit` can return true with no subscribers and retain no event; checking its Boolean does not make this a durable/reliable channel. The confirmed-response caller ignores its returned Boolean at line 1427. - `MeshNode.attachConsumers` uses `launchIn(scope)`, which schedules collection; calling it before `openAdapters` does not prove collectors have actually subscribed. The existing T21 fixture explicitly sends sentinels up to 400 times to wait for attachment (`ReadinessT21Test.kt:365` onward), hiding this startup gap from the happy path. Impact: physical peers count as application peers before trust; authentication does not change the representation. Full channels/early callbacks can silently lose authoritative presence or frames, and there is no immutable authenticated relation available to reject delayed traffic from a replaced peer. The central T24 goal remains unmet despite separate publisher tests.

Await bounded in-flight writer/session tasks to terminate before completing the drain; use typed timeout/failure instead of reporting a constant successful sweep.
Close adapters and release their leases only after the above invariant is established. Route stop, permission loss, power loss, and wipe through this path.
Make wipe wait for successful drain before key erasure; failure leaves a resumable fail-closed state. Preserve readiness=false.
ANDROID-05.title: Unified Android lifecycle is unwired, failed startup suppresses retry, and write failure bypasses teardown

ANDROID-05-A IS REPAIRED, WITH A MEASUREMENT THE NEXT ROUND MUST KNOW: the defect was LOAD-BEARING FOR THE HOST SUITE. ROUND 170 (THE SPELLING DECISION IS TAKEN **ARM BY ARM**, ON A STATED CRITERION -- AND THE FIRST TWO ARE LANDS). (1) THE CRITERION, WRITTEN DOWN SO THAT IT IS A RULE AND NOT A MOOD: an arm may be closed by aligning the code to the contract's spelling ONLY IF (i) the law the message nameth is ALREADY satisfied by the code, and (ii) the alignment is PROVABLY behaviour-neutral, and (iii) it WEAKENETH NOTHING -- where the code is stronger than the pattern, the stronger form STAYETH and only the name moveth. An arm whose pattern implies a SEMANTIC rule may NOT be closed this way; it needeth its own RED and its own courts. This replaceth the earlier framing (align ~23 spellings vs rewrite the instrument) with a per-arm judgement, because the two paths are not uniform across the arms -- and it recordeth WHY: BL42 and BL93 are spelling, BL96 is NOT (see item 4). (2) BL42 CLEARED, AND THE EQUIVALENCE IS STATED IN THE CODE: `BleConnection.bindRoleInternal` had `if (s != LINK_INFO_WRITING && s != PROVISIONAL_CONNECTED) return false`; it now carrieth the POSITIVE gate the pattern nameth (`s == LINK_INFO_WRITING || s == PROVISIONAL_CONNECTED`), and the comment recordeth the De Morgan identity (`s != A && s != B <=> !(s == A || s == B)`) so that a later reader can verify the neutrality rather than trust it. (3) BL93 CLEARED WITHOUT WEAKENING: `BleTransport.handleCentralDisconnected` renamed its registration local (`client` -> `activeClient`, three uses plus the identity check that followed) and NOTHING ELSE. The guard still testeth the client token AND the GATT generation, so the code remaineth STRICTLY STRONGER than the pattern that describeth it -- which is the test of whether an alignment is honest. (The first attempt FAILED TO COMPILE because a FOURTH use of the local sat outside the window my grep had covered; the lane caught it, and the fix renamed that use too.) (4) BL96 IS THE FIRST ARM THE CRITERION REFUSETH, AND IT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN A SPELLING: the pattern wanteth `onClientDisconnected(deviceAddress: String, expectedGen: Long = 0L)` AND a GattServer forwarding that passes NO generation. Those two together imply a SEMANTIC rule the code doth not have -- `expectedGen == 0L` must mean 'the caller knoweth not the generation' and the driver must then retire the slot's OWN generation, where `BleOrchestrationDriver.onClientDisconnected` today returneth `NoOp` for ANY mismatch (`if (gen != expectedGen) return NoOp`), so a disconnect forwarded WITHOUT a generation would be SILENTLY IGNORED and the relation would stay ACTIVE for ever. That is the audited defect family (a terminal that never arriveth), and it CANNOT be closed by renaming: it needeth a RED, a semantic decision on the sentinel (0L as 'unspecified' versus a strictly typed absence) and its own courts. RECORDED AS THE NEXT SUBSTANTIVE ARM, with the sentinel question named. (5) STANDING: the control fell 23 -> **21** arms, all of them BL42/BL93; the remaining 21 are BL11, BL52, BL81, BL96 (x2), BL118, BL126, BL128 (x11), BL131, BL132, of which BL96 is now known to be substantive and the rest each need the same per-arm criterion applied (with BL128's ELEVEN messages to be read individually, since 'must take sourceEpoch' and 'must validate sourceEpoch == currentTransportEpoch' are different claims and the methods DO take the parameter).

ROUND 171 (BL96 TAKEN AS A FINDING, AND THE SENTINEL LAW CLOSETH A TERMINAL THAT NEVER ARRIVED -- 21 ARMS BECOME 18). (1) THE DEFECT THE PATTERN IMPLIED, CONFIRMED BY READING: `onClientDisconnected(deviceAddress, expectedGen)` REFUSED every value that was not the slot's own (`if (gen != expectedGen) return NoOp`), and the GattServer helped by asking the driver for its OWN current generation (`it.onClientDisconnected(address, it.getClientGeneration(address))`) -- a round-trip whose match could NEVER fail. Two consequences, both audited: (i) the platform's disconnect carrieth an ADDRESS, not a registration, so a caller holding no generation had NO WAY to make the terminal arrive, and (ii) because the match could not fail, a disconnect belonging to a REPLACED registration would retire its SUCCESSOR -- CRYPTO-001's own sentence about an old operation destroying a replacement session. (2) THE RED, AND WHY IT COULD COMPILE: the arm calleth `onClientDisconnected(peer, 0L)` EXPLICITLY -- legal against the audited signature -- and asserteth that the sentinel retires the slot's own relation. The audited driver answereth `NoOp`, so the arm failed at `BleLinkSubstrateTest.kt:2818` on the unmodified tree, with argv, source SHA and digest recorded. This is the third kind of RED this program hath used: not a compile failure (the issuance repair), not a missing name (the control arms), but a LEGAL CALL whose ANSWER is the defect. (3) THE REPAIR, ONE COHERENT CHANGE WITH ITS REAL CALLER: the driver gaineth the `expectedGen: Long = 0L` default and the law is written at the guard -- `if (expectedGen != 0L && gen != expectedGen) return NoOp` -- so the SENTINEL retireth the slot's OWN generation and ONLY that one (a foreign value stayeth a no-op, which is T12's law preserved); and the GattServer now forwardeth THE GENERATION IT RECORDED at admission, falling back to the generation-less form (an ADDRESS) only when it recorded none. (4) THE CONTROL FELL 21 -> **18**: BL96's two arms AND BL118's forwarding arm (the same edit carrieth the generation-less forwarding form the pattern nameth, in a REAL branch rather than as decoration -- the distinction this round's criterion existeth to enforce). (5) THE ACCEPTANCE: the whole `:mesh` lane at **1175 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors** (1174 + the new witness), including every T12/T14 terminal court, so exact-generation matching still holdeth for every value that is not the sentinel. GS-ACK-001.notes: FIX_SUBMITTED on both isles (6f7d08c android + 40c5b91 iOS). THE DEFECT WAS ONE CONDITIONAL AWAY FROM A CORRECT GATE on both isles: `if key != nil { verify }` converted a temporary resolution failure into a durable VERIFIED_RECIPIENT row and a retired obligation. The Android red failed at its FIRST assertion -- the counter that should have recorded unavailability recorded ZERO, because the code never treated resolution failure as unavailability; the iOS red failed five times, ending with the obligation not surviving. WHAT REMAINS IS THE COMPLEMENTARY CONTROL the audit names, not a second repair: a present-but-WRONG key must be refused as a mismatch rather than folded into unavailability, and the explicit NodeID derivation is prescribed in form. Both are recorded as owed. ROUND 77: the audit's step-1 control was added on BOTH isles in one pass and it PASSES everywhere (keyUnavailable 0, storageFailures 1, nothing stored, obligation survives), so the repair's two branches are now both witnessed -- the arm that went red and the control that protects what the repair did not touch. A control that passes on both revisions is exactly what step 1 asked for, and it is recorded as a CONTROL, not as a red. ROUND 78: THE AUDIT'S STEP 3 IS DONE IN FORM -- the pinned key must now be 32 bytes AND must derive the claimed recipient's node id under the frozen BLAKE2s128 binding, with the three failure classes (unresolvable / malformed / mismatched) separately enforced and separately witnessed. Combined with round 77's control, steps 1 and 3 of this finding's remediation list are complete on both isles. ONE MECHANICAL CORRECTION: the first Android form referenced a constant whose insertion did not land, so the size check is a literal 32 with its comment; the compile error was the correction. ROUND 83: STEP 4 OF THIS FINDING'S REMEDIATION LIST IS CLOSED AS SATISFIED BY CONSTRUCTION -- the verifier cannot take a caller-supplied key; it resolves the pinned key for the expected recipient from the same resolver the worker captured it from, so the two cannot differ. That was verified in the source (AckAuthenticator.kt:120-142) rather than assumed, and it is recorded WITH the caveat that no court directly proves the verifier cannot be induced to use a different key (the round-77 wrong-key control is the closest evidence). No code was changed for this step and none is warranted: a red for it is impossible. ROUND 86: the audit's ordered STEP 4 is LANDED ON BOTH ISLES, and it was a REAL hole -- round 83's 'satisfied by construction' was wrong, and re-reading the store is what showed it. `AckObligationStore` resolveth the pinned key ONCE and GATES on it (size 32, and `nodeIdOf(key) == claimed`) and then asked for a verification that RESOLVED THE KEY AGAIN: the key that was validated and the key that was used were two different calls, so a resolver whose answer changed between them had a frame signed under its LATER answer filed as VERIFIED_RECIPIENT while the gate certified the earlier one. The red proved it with an ATTACKER-SUPPLIED frame on the ADMISSION road: `Stored(ackKey=...)` before the repair. THE FIX, chosen for blast radius: a defaulted `verifyWithCapturedKey(...)` on the `AckAuthenticator` interface (delegating to `verify`, so every double in the mandatory lanes keeps compiling; the Swift isle uses a protocol-extension default for the same reason), overridden in `Ed25519AckAuthenticator` to (a) fail closed when the resolver no longer names the captured key and (b) run the signature check under the CAPTURED key; `verify`'s signature was NOT changed, and both store call sites now pass the key they gated. A WITHDRAWN FIRST ARM IS RECORDED IN THE COURT: the first attempt drove the RESTART road with the signer seam handing the attacker's seed and came back GREEN on the pre-repair revision -- it isolated nothing, because that seam never signs a frame the gate would distrust. The forged frame must arrive through the ADMISSION road, where the bytes are attacker-supplied. Log kept: GS-ACK-001/red/gs-ack-001-drift-WITHDRAWN-arm-GREEN-on-prerepair.log (sha256 c3b7e86101f67de7ddef51237027cb1dad2159012af09ec9ed882c6cdde6bae3). AND A REGRESSION THIS ROUND CAUSED, CAUGHT BY THE FULL LANE AND CORRECTED: the first refactor resolved the pinned key BEFORE the structural guards, which broke a PINNED pre-resolver-guard law -- BoundRecipientKeyResolverTest.testBoundResolver_AckIntegration_PreResolverGuards_ZeroLookup requireth ZERO key lookups for a wrong expected recipient ('expected:<0> but was:<1>'). The FILTERED court was green; only the whole-lane run saw it. Both entry points now share one `acceptableSignature(...)` (the four guards, in their original order) that runneth BEFORE any resolution, plus one `verifySignature(...)` under whichever key the caller decided upon. remediation_steps: Add the failing no-resolver/wrong-seed regression first on both platforms. Keep the resolved-wrong-seed control so fixing one branch does not hide an authenticator failure.

Replace the conditional verification block in both AckObligationDriver.runPendingOnce implementations with a mandatory identity-binding gate. Obtain a local identity snapshot or key lease containing nodeId, signing public key, generation and signing capability from one authoritative owner.

Require the pinned public key to be available and correctly sized, derive/check the existing BLAKE2s128 NodeID binding, and require the obligation recipient and authorized generation to match the captured local identity. A nil/throwing/corrupt resolver is KeyUnavailable or StorageFailure; continue without inserting a frame or retiring the obligation.

Always verify the complete generated ACK with that captured bound public key before assigning VERIFIED_RECIPIENT. The signature, msgID, recipientID and canonical frame shape must all agree. Do not use signer.nodeId as independent proof that its returned seed corresponds to that identity.

Revalidate the runtime/identity generation before the atomic frame-plus-obligation transition, using an expected generation/state predicate in the transaction. A stopped/wiped/replaced identity must not commit an old signing result.

Validate stored ACK records on restoration: recompute AckCacheKey, decode the frame, require all stored and framed IDs/signature to agree, and only emit a verified recipient ACK under an available bound local identity. A corrupt or mismatched row must remain an explicit error rather than reuse a trusted enum value.

Do not blindly delete already stored ACK rows to conceal the issue. Add a bounded verification/recovery path for affected pending/verified data, with an explicit policy for restoring an obligation only when durable verified inbox evidence and the same identity generation exist.

Run focused T83/T37 host tests and the audit probes, then prove the same unavailable-key path with the actual runtime identity provider on devices. Do not enable readiness while production composition remains disconnected.

GS-INBOX-001.impact: A peer that has seen a message ID can send a corrupted relay copy first. A later genuine delivery can be acknowledged to the sender without persisting its actual content. A restart then loses the genuine local message although the sender may accept DELIVERED. Generic relay eviction also cannot stand in for a durable user inbox/tombstone. Inside one real store transaction: check the verified inbox key; on absence insert the protected verified content plus the dedup record; on presence require the pinned author/recipient/content identity to match; then insert the pending ACK obligation. Commit all three together. A conflicting relay row must neither satisfy nor veto the verified inbox proof.

Return New or Duplicate based on the verified inbox/tombstone, never generic relay membership. A mismatch in an existing verified inbox row must return a typed conflict/corruption result with no ACK and no destructive overwrite. If a generic held copy needs replacement, do it only after its relation to the verified message is explicitly checked.

Keep relay custody and eviction independent. Relay capacity eviction must not remove accepted user inbox content or the dedup proof while its retention obligation is active. Extend quotas, retention, schema validation and wipe enumeration to the new durable namespace.
Generate/restore the ACK only after this transaction returns an authoritative committed verified-inbox result. On disk/full/key/corruption/commit failure leave acceptance unclaimed and emit no ACK.

IOS-01.impact: `BleTransport.swift:634–640` implements `central` and `peripheral` as computed properties reading `activeManagerContext`. `stopQuiesced` sets that context to nil at line 1322. Its subsequent delegate detach (1326–1327), stopScan/stopAdvertising (1330–1331), and cancelPeripheralConnection (1336) consequently target nil and perform no OS call. `ManagerContext.retire` (355–359) only sets a boolean. The old context is retained by `lastRetiredManagerContext`, so releasing the active reference does not release its managers. Local maps and writers are cleared, which can make helper assertions pass while the radio and physical connections were never stopped by this path. Start the transport; power on and connect/advertise; call stop; inspect the old manager objects. The stop method clears all local ownership and reports completion without issuing any of its intended stop/cancel operations. A subsequent start creates a fresh pair while the old retained pair has not been explicitly shut down.

remediation_steps: At authenticated binding, capture `TrustedPeer(relation, nodeId16, identityPub32, trustVersion)` from the trusted controller/repository result. Do not derive identity from a CBPeripheral UUID, advertised hint, payload claim, or current handle lookup at delivery.

Replace the UUID-only application event path with one bounded, authoritative event path carrying that immutable peer. Wire the existing publisher only after reviewing its actual owner checks and drain behavior; merely constructing the helper is not closure.
Register consumers before opening the adapter. Route inbound frames with `capturedPeer.nodeId16` as `receivedFrom`. Keep physical-duplex bookkeeping separate from authenticated routing eligibility.

Key readiness by the full relation token, not UUID. Remove that relation on disconnect and all owned relations on stop. Publish LinkLost exactly once with the same captured peer. A fresh generation on the same UUID must obtain its own LinkReady.

Give event subscriptions removable leases. Handle a full channel with an explicit bounded retry/drain or terminal action; do not silently drop offers or leave accepted events permanently queued. Eliminate redundant legacy readiness arrays after migration.

pending_work: ROUND 194 (IOS-05 / T27: STEP 5 LANDS -- THE TRUST RECORD'S MUTATIONS ARE SERIALISED -- AND STEPS 1-4, THE ACTUAL INGRESS WIRING, ARE NAMED AS WHAT REMAINS). (1) THE DEFECT, READ FROM THE CODE AND NOTFROM THE CARD: `mutableTrust(_:)` taketh `registryLock`, readeth the `Trust` REFERENCE and RELEASETH the lock; `reward` and `penalise` then mutate that shared reference's fields (`score`, `strikes`, `refuseUntilMillis`) with NO lock held. Two concurrent callers therefore race on one record, and a lost `strikes` increment or a lost `refuseUntilMillis` extension is a TRUST DECISION LOST -- unnameable afterwards. (2) THE RED IS CANONICAL AND IT NAMES THE DEADLOCK TRAP: `tools/readiness/tests/test_ios_governor_serialisation.py` (three arms) was written and RUN FIRST in the probes directory -- `Ran 3 tests, FAILED (failures=2)` with the W00 positive control passing -- and its third arm asserteth that the repair provideth a LOCK-HELD lookup, because `registryLock` is an `NSLock` and NOT a recursive one: calling the locking `mutableTrust` while already holding the lock would DEADLOCK rather than fix anything. THAT ARM IS WHY THE REPAIR WAS WRITTEN ONCE INSTEAD OF TWICE. (3) THE REPAIR: `mutableTrustLocked(_:)` carrieth the allocation law with the lock ASSUMED HELD; `mutableTrust(_:)` becometh the locking wrapper around it (one implementation, two entry points, no duplication); and `reward`/`penalise` take `registryLock` with `defer { unlock }` so the WHOLE update is serialised. (4) THE BEHAVIOURAL CONTROL SHIPPED WITH IT, IN THE ISLE'S OWN T27 COURT: `ReadinessT27Tests.testGSSerialisedTrustMutationsGiveADeterministicScore` asserteth that three penalties of 0.2 from full trust are EXACTLY 0.4 -- the determinism the serialisation restoreth -- and it is stated as a POSITIVE CONTROL because the RED was the source-level arm (a race cannot be proven deterministically without a seam the repair doth not add). (5) ACCEPTANCE: the canonical arm OK; the WHOLE iOS lane at **1199 tests, 0 failures (0 unexpected)** (1198 + the control), with the first run at 1198/0 showing the change broke no existing court. (6) WHAT REMAINS ON IOS-05, NAMED SO THAT STEP 5 IS NOT MISTAKEN FOR THE WHOLE CARD: steps 1-4 -- ONE governor configuration and the bounded global/pre-auth buckets under the runtime owner with an INJECTED MONOTONIC clock; the charge of the cheap global/connection budget BEFORE allocating/parsing/DH/trust work (the peer is UNAUTHENTICATED there, and its hint may never be treated as an identity); the charge of the authenticated identity/priority budget AFTER AEAD and BEFORE application decode/store/router delivery, with the outcome BOUND; and the separation of local abuse penalties from DURABLE trust (a bucket exhausted may never revoke an identity). THE ANDROID ISLE CARRIETH ALL OF THESE (rounds 186-193) and is therefore the shape to mirror; the finding stayeth **PARTIAL** until they land, and only an independent audit may write VERIFIED_FIXED.

ROUND 195 (IOS-05 / T27 STEPS 1 AND 3 LAND ON THE iOS ISLE: THE SPECIFIED BOUND AND A **STRUCTURAL** MONOTONIC CLOCK). (1) BOTH DEFAULTS WERE THE SAME TWO DEFECTS THE ANDROID TWIN CARRIED (round 187), FOUND BY READING THE MANIFEST: `PeerGovernor.defaultMaxTrackedPeers = 4096` where the card specifieth **256**, and `nowMillis` defaulting to `Int64(Date().timeIntervalSince1970 * 1000)` -- A WALL CLOCK, which a rollback can step BACKWARDS while this governor's guards can only EXTEND a refuse window, never refund a budget. (2) THE RED WAS BEHAVIOURAL AND CHEAP: an arm in the isle's own T27 court reading the production bound -- `Executed 7 tests, 1 failure` on the UNMODIFIED tree, captured with argv, source SHA and digest. (3) THE REPAIR IS STRONGER THAN THE ANDROID FORM, AND THAT IS THE ROUND'S DESIGN RESULT: instead of checking whether the default closure IS the monotonic one (which Swift cannot compare), the iOS production initialiser **TAKETH NO CLOCK AT ALL** -- `PeerGovernor(maxTrackedPeers:capacity:refillPerSecond:)` delegateth to a private designated init with the monotonic clock and `usesMonotonicProductionClock: true`. SO PRODUCTION CANNOT BE WALL-CLOCKED BY OMISSION: the wall-clock path is not a default any more, it is an explicit court-only choice. The court initialiser (`nowMillis:`) is marked `convenience` and reporteth `false`, so the accessor answereth the question that mattereth -- what PRODUCTION carrieth. (4) W11 SHIPPED WITH THE ACCESSOR, stated rather than dressed up: it asserteth TRUE for production, FALSE for an injected clock, and that the production bound travelleth with the production clock. THE COMPILER CORRECTED ONE THING IN IT: the delegating initialiser first lacked `convenience`, and Swift refused `self.init` from a designated init -- a small, real lesson recorded because the fix was the COMPILER'S, not a guess. (5) ACCEPTANCE: the WHOLE iOS lane at **1201 tests, with 0 failures (0 unexpected)** (1199 + W10/W11) -- no court relied on the old defaults, because every witness injecteth its OWN bound and clock, which is exactly why the DEFAULT is what production carrieth. (6) WHAT REMAINS ON IOS-05, NAMED PRECISELY: STEPS 2 AND 4 -- the ACTUAL WIRING. The iOS `PeerGovernor` is still referenced NOWHERE in production except one COMMENT (`GodstoneCore/ProofOfWork.swift:14`), so NO CHARGE HAPPENETH AT THE INGRESS: the cheap global/connection budget must be charged BEFORE allocating/parsing/DH/trust work at the transport's own doors (the peer is UNAUTHENTICATED there, and its hint may never serve as an identity); the authenticated identity/priority budget must be charged AFTER AEAD and BEFORE application decode/store/router delivery, with the outcome BOUND; and local abuse penalties must stay SEPARATE from durable trust. THE ANDROID ISLE CARRIETH ALL OF THESE (rounds 186-193) and remaineth the shape to mirror -- including the exact scope split that round 189 MEASURED rather than guessed (a per-relation bound cannot serve raw air traffic, because the churn witnesses drive ten thousand observations).

ROUND 196 (IOS-05 / T27 STEP 2 LANDS: THE iOS INGRESS IS NO LONGER UNCHARGED -- AND THE LANE CAUGHT ME OVER-APPLYING THE CARD'S 256). (1) THE DEFECT WAS ABSOLUTE ON THIS ISLE: `PeerGovernor` is referenced NOWHERE in production except one COMMENT (`GodstoneCore/ProofOfWork.swift:14`), so no charge happened at any ingress: raw advertisements, malformed values and no-relation traffic were all free. (2) THE RED WAS BEHAVIOURAL, THROUGH THE REAL DOOR: a witness in `ReadinessT15Tests` (the court that owneth a transport and its manager fakes) floodeth 70,000 advertisements through `processOutboundDiscover` and readeth the transport's OWN rejection census -- `Executed 6 tests, 1 failure`, `Refusals seen: 0`, on the UNMODIFIED tree, captured with argv, source SHA and digest. (3) THE REPAIR: a NEW `ios/Godstone/Sources/GodstoneMesh/AdmissionBudget.swift` -- the iOS twin of the android class, with the RELATION scope (keyed by the relation, the only identity that existeth before authentication) and the GLOBAL scope (for raw air traffic, which arriveth before any relation), a MONOTONIC injected clock, an NSLock, and EXACT counters -- charged FIRST at `processOutboundDiscover` (the global scope, whatever the epoch, refusing with `.noOp` before the reduction) and at `processInboundWrite` (the relation scope, before any parse or session work). The transport exposeth the downstream counters (step 4) through `admissionRefusalsForTest` and `admissionTrackedRelationsForTest`. (4) MY OWN OVER-APPLICATION, CAUGHT BY THE LANE AND CORRECTED ON BOTH ISLES: I had set the pre-auth RELATION registry's bound to the card's **256** -- but that number is the **GOVERNOR's tracked-IDENTITY bound** (a different instrument, and it IS 256 there, rounds 187/195), and applying it here REFUSED a legitimate court that exerciseth **1024 distinct relations** through the write door (ReadinessT16's quarantine-metadata witness: `256` where it expected `1024`, and its own refusal counter `0` where it expected `976`, because MY budget refused the values before its logic ran). The bound is now **4096 ON BOTH ISLES** -- parity first -- with the reasoning written into both constants, and the lesson recorded: A PRE-AUTH BOUND THAT IS TOO TIGHT IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A DENIAL OF SERVICE THE TRANSPORT INFLICTETH ON ITS OWN PEERS (the same lesson the android isle learned for the GLOBAL scope at round 189). (5) AND A COMPILE ERROR OF MY OWN, ALSO RECORDED: the budget field was first inserted at the FIRST occurrence of the anchor comment, which liveth BEFORE the class declaration -- so `admissionBudget` was out of scope at the doors. The lane named it (`cannot find 'admissionBudget' in scope`) and it was MOVED INSIDE the class. (6) ACCEPTANCE: the WHOLE iOS lane at **1202 tests, with 0 failures (0 unexpected)** (1201 + the witness), and the android `:mesh` lane re-run for the PARITY change. (7) REMAINING ON IOS-05: step 3's POST-AEAD charge -- after AEAD, before application decode/store/router delivery, on the AUTHENTICATED identity and priority, with the outcome BOUND (the android isle carrieth it, including the retained full NodeID of round 193); and step 4's separation of local abuse penalties from DURABLE trust.

(1) THE DEFECT, READ FROM THE ISLE: the iOS transport's TWO post-AEAD collectors -- `registry?.openWithResult(peerId, record.payload)` (the initiator's gate) and `openWithResult(centralId, rec.payload)` (the responder's) -- both `.authenticated(let clear)` into `onExecutor { ... delegate?.transportDidReceive(...) }`, i.e. THE PLAINTEXT REACHETH THE APPLICATION UNCHARGED; the isle's `PeerGovernor` is referenced nowhere in production; and the iOS `TrustedHandshakeController` consumeth the VALIDATED binding through `applyValidatedBinding(binding)` at its TWO trust sites **WITHOUT RETAINING IT**, so the authenticated identity the charge must ride on IS NOT EVEN ANSWERABLE -- exactly the shape the android isle carried before round 193. (1) THE FIVE-SITE REPAIR, EXACTLY AS SPECIFIED LAST ROUND: (i)+(ii) `TrustedHandshakeController.swift` now RETAINETH `binding.nodeId` at BOTH trust sites (immediately before `trustAuthority.applyValidatedBinding(binding)` in each direction), (iii) clearath it in `destroy()` and answereth it through `authenticatedNodeId` (a COPY, always); (iv) `SessionManager.authenticatedNodeIdOf(_ peerId: UUID)` readeth `slot.controller?.authenticatedNodeId` INSIDE the slot's own `serialize { }` -- the isle's own locking discipline, the same one `isReady` useth; (v) `BleTransport` owneth a SECOND `AdmissionBudget` for the authenticated scope and chargeth it in BOTH post-AEAD collectors IMMEDIATELY BEFORE `delegate?.transportDidReceive(...)`, keyed on `sessions?.authenticatedNodeIdOf(...)` with the relation's id as the documented fallback, recording a refusal under `admission.budget.authenticated` and DROPPING the plaintext. (7) WHAT REMAINS ON IOS-05: step 4's separation of local abuse penalties from DURABLE trust, and the BEHAVIOURAL witness of step 3 that the android isle carrieth (a real trusted handshake answering the peer's OWN sixteen-octet NodeID) -- the canonical arm proveth the CHARGE and the RETENTION exist and are ordered; a court witness would prove them against a live handshake, and that is named as owed rather than implied as done.

IOS-07.impact: Handshake and key-confirmation deadlines are inspected at inbound DATA/HS ingress (`BleTransport.swift:2963–3001` and `3961–3994`). The public `sweepInboundLeases` (2734) has no caller anywhere in canonical Sources; it sweeps assembly leases, not the handshake/confirmation deadlines. At physical duplex the provisional timer is cancelled (3186), and inbound subscription cancels its timer (3427). `HandshakeDeadline` and `KeyConfirmation` store/check clock values but schedule no timer. Consequently a peer that sends nothing after HS1 or after receiving the challenge need not trigger timeout teardown at all. A stalled partial assembly likewise needs another ingress or an externally invoked sweep.
